mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of Chusik Hoesa (Certified Corporate Registration Record, Deung-gi Sa-hang Jeon-bu Jeung-myeong)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registration Office, Court Administration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel exclusive route A for Hague Apostille states: obtain sealed certified copy from the Korean court registry, then obtain Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea, and submit directly to the receiving registrar. Parallel exclusive route B for non-member states: obtain sealed certified copy, obtain MOFA authentication, then consular legalization by the embassy/consulate of the destination state; Apostille must never be combined with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Tax Compliance Certificate and Active Corporate Registration Search)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea and the competent District Court Registration Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel exclusive route A: obtain original tax compliance certificate and court certificate, have notary public certify signatures if required, obtain Apostille from MOFA, submit directly. Parallel exclusive route B for non-member states: notarize, MOFA authentication, destination embassy consular legalization; no sequential use of Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Incorporation, Bank Account Opening, and Offshore Development Center Administration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Chusik Hoesa, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel exclusive route A: notarize original signatures, obtain MOFA Apostille, submit directly. Parallel exclusive route B for non-member states: notarize, MOFA authentication, destination consular legalization; never chain the two methods.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Jeong-gwan) of the Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators and initial directors, filed with the Korean court registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel exclusive route A: certified copy from court registry; notarize any signed pages if required; MOFA Apostille. Parallel exclusive route B: certified copy; MOFA authentication; destination consular legalization; do not use Apostille for non-member states.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter and Professional Client Due Diligence Confirmation from a Licensed Korean Commercial Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate relationship manager of a licensed commercial bank in Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel exclusive route A: bank letter on bank letterhead, officer signature and corporate seal; notarize officer signature; MOFA Apostille; submit directly. Parallel exclusive route B: notarize, MOFA authentication, destination consular legalization; never chain Apostille with consular legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, UBOs, directors, and signatories must be screened before engagement and again on each change against the OFAC SDN list, the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Republic of Korea s domestic financial sanctions list maintained by the Financial Services Commission and KoFIU under the Act on Reporting and Use. Screening must cover exact name, aliases, transliterations, national ID, passport numbers, and a phonetic fuzzy-match library. Any confirmed hit mandates Suspicious Transaction Report and provisional asset freeze. Foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, international-organization PEPs, their family members and close associates require enhanced due diligence, documentation of source of wealth and source of funds, senior-management approval, and at least semiannual periodic review. Negative news and adverse-media checks by independent databases are also mandatory.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (Internet Deung-gi-so), official national court registration portal, and National Tax Service HomeTax System for pre-incorporation taxpayer name verification
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean commercial law requires the official corporate name to be expressed in the Korean script; a Latin-script brand must be transliterated into Korean Hangul for the registered name, and the English spelling can be recorded as a secondary name. The four-tier naming formula is: (1) distinctive brand or trade name; (2) description of principal business object; (3) the mandatory entity suffix Chusik Hoesa; and (4) optional English alias in parentheses. Registry staff compare names on identity of pronunciation, shape, and likely deception, not only exact text.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: When a proposed name is refused by the Korean Internet Registration Office, the rejection notice will cite the specific statutory ground, typically identity or confusing similarity under Commercial Act Articles 22 and 23. The applicant may, within 14 days from notice, submit through the same portal a written objection with a comparison table, evidence of trademark coexistence, or a revised transliteration. If the registration office maintains the rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the head of the registration office and, failing that, seek review by the local District Court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure within 20 days. The original name reservation window may be extended once by 15 days for a material modification if requested in writing before expiration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services are technically acceptable for the court mailing address of a Chusik Hoesa, but Korean tax and banking practice imposes substance conditions. The National Tax Service will not recognize a post-office box or mail-forwarding only address as the place of effective management if directors, employees, books, and server infrastructure are not evident. For an Offshore Development Center, banks and tax authorities will require a physical lease (even co-working), domain email, payroll, signed client contracts, and project artifacts located in Korea. A virtual office without any of these creates tax residency ambiguity and may result in registration cancellation, refusal of VAT zero-rating, or denial of bank account opening. Practical minimum: lease a qualified commercial space of at least 20 square meters, install a nameplate, and maintain operational records on site.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) lease contract and deposit schedule; (2) statutory corporate nameplate at entrance; (3) office key cards or CCTV; (4) business cards and corporate email domain; (5) employee employment contracts and payroll journal; (6) code repositories, servers, and helpdesk tickets evidencing actual software engineering; (7) board resolutions approving budget and business plan; (8) corporate seal and register of shareholders. Quantitative risk for a new ODC with modest share capital: 8-12 percent in the first year; rising to 18-25 percent if claiming zero-rated VAT refunds, treaty benefits, or inward remittance anomalies; unannounced visits by municipal tax inspectors are more plausible than registry inspections.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Korean Supreme Court Court Administration Office (free public search; no separate official name-reservation fee for Chusik Hoesa incorporation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official statutory tariff: no fee for online name search; no separate name-reservation fee before filing incorporation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate registration license tax and local education surcharge on Chusik Hoesa incorporation registration (based on paid-in capital of USD 50,000 equivalent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Metropolitan city/county local government tax office (through the court registration collection system)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Local Tax Act tariff: license tax 0.4 percent of stated capital plus 20 percent education surcharge; approximate for a USD 50,000 capital base.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Court registration filing fee for incorporation of Chusik Hoesa (commercial registry entry)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: District Court Registration Office, Court Administration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Court Fees Act schedule for incorporation registration of a stock corporation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Articles of Association, Board Resolution, Power of Attorney, and certified true copies for the legalization bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary Public Act statutory scale for document notarization; market benchmark USD 150 to 250 per corporate pack.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal fee for incorporation, statutory corporate governance, name clearance, preparation of the documents, and AML/UBO screening oversight
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark fixed fee for standard Chusik Hoesa with no minimum capital; no statutory tariff applies.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Comprehensive AML/KYC, PEP, OFAC, UN, EU, and Korean FSI sanctions database screening for UBOs, directors, and signatories (initial run and reports for two cycles)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial data providers such as Refinitiv World-Check, LexisNexis, and local credit bureau
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per screening record; no statutory tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office address and operational substance package (co-working lease, nameplate, registration mail handling, and business address for twelve months)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed registered-office service provider and co-working landlord
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark USD 100 per month for commercial registered-office service without physical floor area; higher if meeting room included.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), specifically Articles 288 through 317 (Incorporation of Stock Companies), Article 289 (Articles of Incorporation), Article 295 (Subscription of Shares), Article 302 (Incorporation Meeting), and Article 317 (Registration of Incorporation).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local District Court Registry (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registry, Corporate Registration Division) under the jurisdiction of the company's registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan) and Application for Registration of Incorporation (Changui Deunggi) filed with the court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act does not impose a minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa. However, the total issued shares must be fully paid in at incorporation, and the subscription price must be deposited into a bank account in the name of the company (or a designated account) before registration. No escrow account is required beyond this deposit.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (CHUSIK HOESA) ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A MEETING PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 391-2 OF THE KOREAN COMMERCIAL ACT

WHEREAS, [Company Name] (the 'Company') was incorporated under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea on [Date], with its registered office at [Address], and its Articles of Incorporation duly authorized and executed;

WHEREAS, the initial directors of the Company, as named in the Articles of Incorporation, have been duly elected and have accepted their appointments;

WHEREAS, the Company has issued [Number] shares of common stock at a par value of KRW [Amount] per share, and the total subscription price of KRW [Total] has been fully paid in and deposited in the Company's designated bank account as required by Article 295 of the Commercial Act;

WHEREAS, the Board deems it necessary and in the best interests of the Company to adopt certain foundational resolutions to commence business operations, including the appointment of statutory officers, the adoption of a registered office, and the authorization of banking arrangements;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ISSUANCE: The Board hereby ratifies and confirms the issuance and subscription of [Number] shares of common stock, each with a par value of KRW [Amount], for a total paid-in capital of KRW [Total]. The Board acknowledges that all subscription amounts have been fully deposited in the Company's bank account at [Bank Name], Account Number [Account], and that the deposit certificate has been obtained and will be filed with the registration application.

2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The Board hereby adopts and confirms the registered office of the Company at [Full Address], Republic of Korea, as the principal place of business and statutory seat for all legal and administrative purposes. The Board authorizes the Chief Executive Officer to execute any lease agreements or other documents necessary to maintain such office.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby authorizes the opening and maintenance of corporate bank accounts with [Bank Name] and any other financial institutions as may be necessary. The Board designates the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer as the sole authorized signatories for all banking transactions, with the power to execute checks, wire transfers, and other financial instruments, subject to the Company's internal approval policy requiring dual signatures for amounts exceeding KRW [Threshold].

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board hereby appoints the following individuals to the statutory offices of the Company: (a) [Name] as Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Representative Director, with full authority to represent the Company in all matters and to execute contracts on behalf of the Company; (b) [Name] as Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and Director, with authority over financial affairs and treasury management; and (c) [Name] as Auditor (Gamsa), who shall be independent and not an employee of the Company, to oversee compliance with the Commercial Act and internal controls. Each officer shall serve until the next annual general meeting of shareholders or until their successors are duly elected.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby authorizes the CEO and CFO, jointly or severally, to take all necessary actions, execute all documents, and make all filings required to effectuate the resolutions herein, including but not limited to the registration of incorporation with the competent court registry, the issuance of business registration certificates with the tax authorities, and the opening of any additional bank accounts.

6. EFFECTIVE DATE: These resolutions shall be effective immediately upon adoption.

ADOPTED this [Day] day of [Month], [Year], by the unanimous written consent of all directors, in accordance with Article 391-2 of the Commercial Act.

[Signature of Director 1]
[Signature of Director 2]
[Signature of Director 3]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (Bunseo) in the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation (Jeongjin) in Korean, including mandatory clauses: company name, purpose (including offshore software development and IT services), registered office address, total authorized shares, par value, names and addresses of incorporators, and method of public notice. The document must be signed by all incorporators and notarized by a Korean notary public. The notary will verify the identity of the incorporators and the legality of the clauses. After notarization, obtain a certified copy of the notarized articles. This step is a prerequisite for the subsequent registration application.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID copies of all incorporators
Power of attorney if any incorporator is represented
Proof of address of registered office (e.g., lease agreement or title deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects in the articles (e.g., missing mandatory clauses), amend the draft and resubmit. If the notary requires additional identification, provide certified translations or apostilled documents. Typically, corrections are resolved within 1-2 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Subscription Price and Obtain Deposit Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Bank in Korea (e.g., Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary bank account in the name of the company (or the incorporators) and deposit the full subscription price for all issued shares. The deposit must be made before the registration application. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit (Yejigeum Jeungmyeongseo) confirming the amount and the account holder. This certificate is a mandatory attachment to the registration application. Ensure the deposit is made in KRW and that the account name matches the intended company name (or the incorporators' names). The certificate must be dated within 30 days of the registration filing.
required_dossiers: Identification of the person making the deposit
Certificate of deposit issued by the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open an account due to incomplete documentation, provide the missing items (e.g., proof of address). If the deposit certificate is lost, request a reissue from the bank, which typically takes 1 business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Application for Registration of Incorporation with Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registry (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Registration of Incorporation (Chokui Deungnam) to the court registry having jurisdiction over the registered office. The application must include the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the deposit certificate, the list of directors and auditor, and the written consent of each director to accept office. The court will review the documents for compliance with the Commercial Act. Upon approval, the court will issue a Certificate of Registration (Deunggi Jeungmyeongseo). This step is the formal legal incorporation of the company.
required_dossiers: Certificate of deposit of subscription price
List of directors and auditor with their consent letters
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a query or suspension (e.g., missing signature), correct the deficiency within the given period (usually 2 weeks). If the application is rejected, file an appeal or resubmit with the required corrections. The court registry provides a written notice of reasons for rejection, and the applicant may cure within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Business Registration Certificate from Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office (National Tax Service)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the court registration certificate, apply for a Business Registration Certificate (Saeopja Deungrokjeung) at the local tax office within 20 days of incorporation. Submit the court registration certificate, the company's articles, and identification of the CEO. The tax office will issue a business registration number (10-digit) and certificate. This certificate is required for opening bank accounts, issuing tax invoices, and conducting business. The tax office may also register the company for VAT and corporate income tax.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requests additional information (e.g., proof of office lease), provide the documents within 5 business days. If the application is delayed, follow up with the tax office or use the online HomeTax system to track status.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Bank Account and Appoint Statutory Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Bank and Company Board of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the company's name using the business registration certificate and court registration certificate. The bank will conduct due diligence (AML/KYC) and may require the board resolution authorizing the account signatories. Simultaneously, convene a board meeting (or obtain written consent) to formally appoint the CEO, CFO, and Auditor as per the pro-forma resolution. File the appointment with the court registry if required (for auditor, within 2 weeks). Ensure all statutory officers have signed acceptance letters.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional documentation (e.g., proof of business purpose), provide the ISIC 6202 description and contracts. If the board resolution is challenged, hold a formal meeting and record minutes. For auditor appointment, file with the court registry within 2 weeks to avoid penalties.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating the HomeTax electronic portal (www.hometax.go.kr) and the EDI customs-trade linkage systems. Foreign non-resident entities file through the competent district tax office or the Seoul National Tax Service International Tax Affairs Division, using the NTS HomeTax online filing gateway and Tax Call Center 126.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Chusik Hoesa (Stock Corporation) forming the Offshore Development Center, the domestic corporate TIN/VAT ID is the 10-digit Business Registration Number (Saupja Deungnok Beonho) issued by the district tax office after formal corporation registration with the court registry. The application must be submitted within 20 days of business commencement using the NTS Business Registration Application (Saupja Deungnok Shincheongseo), accompanied by the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, court registration certificate, office lease documentation, identity documents of the representative, and any applicable foreign investment report. For a non-resident foreign entity that is not a domestic corporation, the foreign enterprise must appoint a tax representative in Korea with a domestic place of business, submit the same Business Registration Application, attach apostilled or consular-legalized foreign registration certificates, a power of attorney and certificate of tax representative appointment, and evidence of a place of business in Korea; upon approval, the NTS issues the Business Registration Certificate which constitutes the unified corporate TIN and VAT registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity elections for a Chusik Hoesa. The entity is mandatorily treated as a domestic corporation subject to entity-level corporation tax on worldwide income; no passthrough election is available to a limited stock corporation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean VAT Act and its Enforcement Decree, administered through the National Tax Service HomeTax e-invoicing network.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover-based exemption for legal persons; VAT registration is mandatory upon business commencement within 20 days. A separate simplified VAT filing threshold of KRW 80,000,000 in annual taxable supplies applies to eligible small businesses but does not suspend or eliminate VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korean VAT taxpayers must issue electronic tax invoices (e-Ssuin) through HomeTax and transmit them to the NTS by the day following issuance. The NTS performs near real-time electronic clearance and cross-validation of e-invoicing against VAT returns through EDI/API connectivity for enterprise taxpayers; there is no government-issued physical anti-fraud stamp or pre-clearance stamping requirement, but delayed, omitted, or mismatched e-invoices trigger automated NTS audit flags, penalty assessments, and cases are sent to the risk-analytics system for compliance review.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under the Korean VAT Act and Enforcement Decree for goods physically exported and for services exported in exchange for foreign currency. For the ISIC 6202 offshore software engineering and maintenance hub, zero-rating is substantiated when the software development, support, or maintenance services are supplied to a foreign principal, are actually performed and consumed outside Korea or are confirmed as offshore services falling within the statutory zero-rated foreign-currency-earning service categories, and the foreign currency consideration is received from abroad in Korea. The supplier must be a registered Korean entity, must issue an electronic tax invoice marked as zero-rated export supply, and must maintain contemporaneous evidence that the recipient is a non-resident, the services are rendered offshore, and the proceeds are repatriated to Korea.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic Export Customs Declaration (EDI Export Bill of Entry) where physical goods, media, or tangible deliverables are exported
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill if physical goods are shipped from Korea
Signed Offshore Software Development Agreement and Statement of Work identifying the foreign contracting party
Service completion report, acceptance certificate, or deliverable handover sign-off evidencing offshore performance
Commercial invoice and zero-rated electronic tax invoice (e-Ssuin) distinctly marked as zero-rated export supply
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Certificate of Foreign Exchange Receipt issued by a Korean foreign-exchange bank showing receipt of the foreign currency consideration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service cross-check export declarations, e-invoices, service contracts, and bank foreign-exchange receipts. If a zero-rated export claim is not supported by the required documentation, NTS reclassifies the supply as taxable domestic supply and assesses the 10% VAT not paid, together with an under-reporting penalty of 10% for negligent underpayment and up to 40% for fraudulent or unjustified omission under the Framework Act on National Taxes, plus daily late-payment surcharges at the statutory rate until payment is made. Any previously claimed VAT refund is clawed back with interest, deliberate fabrication of export-support documents may result in criminal liability under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, and the entity may be disqualified from future zero-rating and targeted for intensive export VAT auditing.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) / Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized current account and a largely liberalized capital account with residual administrative screening. The Korean won is freely convertible for underlying trade, services, and dividend remittance once the bank reporting requirements are met. However, capital account inflows and outflows require Foreign Exchange Information Network (FEIIN) reporting, statement of purpose, and in specific cases pre-registration or approval from the Ministry of Economy and Finance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted after the completion of external audit and National Tax Service clearance on corporate income tax and withholding tax; the remitting bank will verify the audited financial statements, board resolution on dividends, shareholder register, and the applicable withholding tax payment. There is no mandatory export proceeds surrender ratio; exporters may keep hard currency in domestic foreign-currency accounts or convert to Korean won. The deep interbank spot and forward liquidity of the KRW/USD market, alongside the availability of commercial cross-currency swap lines, makes the Korean won one of the most efficiently routed Asian currencies for a structured offshore software engineering entity. Yet the strict FEIIN declaration timeline and the physical presence expectations for senior officers remain the most frequent treasury onboarding friction points. Therefore the entity should maintain all capital and operational documentation in a continuous compliance file accessible to the Korean bank relationship manager.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be collected within six months from the date of export performance (service delivery or software milestone acceptance). No fixed surrender percentage applies currently; proceeds may either be retained in a domestic foreign-currency account or exchanged into Korean won. All receipts need to be routed through a licensed foreign exchange bank and reported via the Foreign Exchange Information Network (FEIIN) by the statutory deadline (typically the 25th day of the following month). Overdue receivables require a written extension application indicating justifiable cause and a proposed collection schedule.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, only Korean-licensed foreign exchange banks can legally complete statutory FX transactions and capital receipts. Offshore FinTech/EMI platforms such as Wise for Business and Payoneer are not licensed as local banks and therefore cannot be used for statutory capital injection, capital verification, or the primary treasury clearing rail for the ODC entity. They may only be used as an auxiliary collection gateway for open-account service invoices from non-Korean clients, and even then the underlying receivable should still be settled into a Korean bank account when timing of tax benefits or transfer pricing is required. For a Payment Institution license, domestic fintechs (for example Tosspayments or Naver Pay) can handle local merchant acquiring but not cross-border treasury settlement for a non-resident owned IT services company without partnering with a Tier-1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory. At least one registered representative or a locally authorised officer with a broad power of attorney must appear physically in the Korean bank's branch for the KYC interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not recognised for the primary signatory; however, a notarised power of attorney can be prepared at the Korean Embassy and apostilled, allowing the appointed local officer or director to attend the interview on behalf of the foreign statutory director. The bank will also require the foreign beneficial owners' certified passport copies, corporate registration excerpts from the overseas parent registry, and a factual business statement explaining the ODC service scope, headcount, payee profile and forecast SWIFT traffic. Some banks will accept an e-KYC selfie step for supplementary signers, but the authorized representative must still appear in-branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial ownership opacity when the parent entity is incorporated in a zero/low-tax jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide notarised and apostilled UBO declaration, group registry excerpt showing the ownership chain up to the individual, passport copies of the ultimate individuals, CRS and FATCA self-certifications, and ninety-day utility/residence records to show actual management location.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incongruent seed capital injection or lack of proof for the source of funds during the capital increase registration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply audited global accounts of the overseas parent, six-month bank statements for the remitting account, intercompany loan agreement or equity investment board resolution, and the Korean-side foreign currency purchase application with the purpose code for capital acquisition.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between intragroup software service invoices and economic substance, raising transfer pricing and false documentation concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a complete transfer pricing report, executed service-level agreement, staffing schedule, detailed timesheets and GitHub/Jira activity logs of the ODC engineers, milestone acceptance certificates, and a monthly invoice register aligned with headcount and body-hour rates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Contradictory cross-border payment routing or unexpected counterparties on clearing rails.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a know-your-counterparty file with official registry extract and beneficial owner list of each counterparty, sanctions and PEP screening results, reference letters or bank confirmation from the counterparty's bank, SWIFT copy of the prior transactions, and a narrative reconciliation of each payment to an underlying contract and delivery proof.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital must be routed by SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the overseas parent to the designated Korean Tier-1 bank's foreign currency account opened in the ODC's name. The remittance narrative must show the FEIIN purpose code for corporate capital acquisition or equity injection and the reference to the paid-in capital registration. Upon receipt, the bank will issue a foreign exchange purchase or receipt certificate, convert the funds into KRW when required, and file the FEIIN report. For statutory capital verification, the company must complete the capital registration with the court registry office and deliver the bank-issued certificate of capital reservation together with the board resolution and the foreign investor's identity documents.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operational trade settlements, the entity will use: (1) SWIFT MT103 for monthly open-account service invoices owed by the overseas parent or end-client; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit for hardware or software license purchases requiring a payment undertaking; and (3) documentary collections for milestone-based deliverables with contractual bill-of-lading or acceptance certificate. All outgoing wires must reference the underlying Korean FEIIN purpose code for service cost or goods trade, be supported by an invoice and delivery proof, and be reported within the FEIIN monthly filing window.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD forward contracts with licensed Korean banks, covering forecasted export software development receivables and intercompany settlements, with maturity not exceeding 12 months and underlying trade documentation.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on KRW for the offshore parent or international payment intermediaries where settlement is made in a convertible currency without won delivery, authorised under non-resident hedging rules.

Cross-currency swaps (USD/KRW) used solely to hedge the principal and interest of intercompany borrowings or the foreign investor's equity bridge, with bank confirmation that the swap is linked to an underlying receivable or capital flow and not a standalone speculative position.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting notice, holding of meeting, approval of financial statements, approval of external audit report, and approval of statutory internal auditor report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing is required; minutes are retained on-site in the corporate minute book, and any resulting director or representative-director change is separately registered with the competent Korean Commercial Registration Court
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months of fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, on or before March 31 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Violation of the Korean Commercial Act AGM timing rule exposes responsible directors to administrative fines up to KRW 20,000,000 (approximately USD 14,600); repeated failure to hold the AGM or to approve financial statements can trigger a mandatory tax audit and loss of tax clearance certificates, and if an abandoned corporation fails to maintain legal existence, the competent court may order administrative strike-off or judicial dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External audit report and audited financial statements submitted electronically where the Chusik Hoesa is subject to the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system, with the report also delivered to shareholders at the Annual General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited financial statements must be finalized before the AGM required by March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end; the audit report, once received by the company, must be filed with the FSS DART system within seven calendar days of receipt
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission or late submission to the FSS can result in administrative penalties up to KRW 30,000,000 (approximately USD 22,000), disciplinary action against directors and the external auditor, designation as a public-interest audit company, and in severe cases regulatory orders that can suspend business operations; persistent abandonment of audit obligations is an administrative strike-off trigger in conjunction with tax registration cancellation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and corporate income tax self-assessment for the Chusik Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through HomeTax electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 of the year following a December 31 fiscal year-end; for a non-calendar fiscal year-end, the filing is due within three months after the close of the fiscal year; a previously approved extension of up to two months is available in limited circumstances
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers an additional tax of 20 percent of the unpaid tax for non-filing, and unfaithful or fraudulent under-reporting triggers additional tax of 10 percent to 40 percent of the under-reported tax base; statutory interest accrues from the original due date at the annual rate prescribed by the Framework Act on National Taxes; chronic delinquency leads to asset seizure, freezing of tax clearance certificates, administrative cancellation of the business registration, and if no business activity exists, administrative strike-off of the corporate entity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local income tax return and payment of the local surtax on corporate income tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government of the jurisdiction where the registered head office is located (Si, Gun, or Gu) through the WETAX local tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same due date as the corporate income tax return, being March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the Local Tax Act, failure to file or under-reporting the local income tax surcharge triggers an additional tax of 20 percent of the unpaid local tax plus local tax interest; prolonged non-payment permits local government seizure of bank accounts and receivables, refusal of tax clearance certificates, and administrative cancellation of the business registration, ultimately supporting an administrative strike-off or forced collection process

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment and beneficial-ownership change report for non-resident shareholders, including any share transfer, equity contribution change, or major ownership movement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through KOTRA or a designated foreign exchange bank; beneficial ownership alerts are separately reported through the company's AML financial institution relationship
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days of any triggering event such as a share transfer, capital increase, or change in effective beneficial ownership; there is no annual UBO confirmation if no ownership event occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a Foreign Investment Promotion Act change report can result in fines up to KRW 10,000,000 (approximately USD 7,300) and loss of foreign-investor treaty and statutory protections; failure to refresh beneficial-ownership information for AML purposes can expose the company to regulatory censure, restrictions on banking services, and mandatory administrative compliance orders, and extreme abandonment can contribute to administrative strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Chusik Hoesa must appoint an independent certified public accountant and undergo a statutory external audit if total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 8.8 million). The audit trigger is primarily balance-sheet asset-based, not turnover or headcount-based; however, independent CPA audit is also mandatory without regard to the asset threshold for listed companies, companies whose securities will be listed or traded on a Korean securities exchange, financial companies and institutions under the Financial Services Commission, and any company specifically designated by the Financial Services Commission as a public-interest or externally audit-required entity. Companies below the KRW 12 billion asset threshold are exempt from mandatory statutory external audit unless they fall within one of the mandatory designation categories.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) apply to listed companies and certain financial institutions. For non-listed Chusik Hoesa subject to the external audit law, management may apply K-IFRS or Korean GAAP under the Statements of Korea Accounting Standards, while qualifying small companies may apply the Korean SME accounting standards. All annual financial statements used for statutory purposes must be prepared on an accrual basis, stated in Korean won, and reconciled to taxable income in the corporate tax return filed with the National Tax Service.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not require an annual UBO calendar filing for an ordinary private Chusik Hoesa. Instead, the foreign-investor shareholding and beneficial-ownership change protocol requires a report to MOTIE/KOTRA within 30 days of any share transfer, capital movement, or change in effective beneficial ownership. The company must immediately update its shareholder registry and make corresponding entries in the board and shareholder minutes. For AML purposes, beneficial owners must be verified whenever a financial relationship or transaction triggers customer due diligence, and a corporate secretarial annual refresh should include a board-approved ownership declaration to confirm the register of members remains accurate. If the company is a listed issuer or falls under capital market disclosure rules, substantial shareholding changes must additionally be reported to the Financial Services Commission within the statutory five-day or ten-day disclosure window, as applicable.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and share transfer records
Register of Charges and Mortgages over company assets
Minutes of shareholders meetings and board of directors meetings (Minute Book)
Statutory accounting books, source vouchers, and tax reconciliation records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 - USD 30,000 per annum if mandatory; USD 0 if the entity is below the statutory asset threshold and has no public-interest designation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% statutory top national corporate income tax rate for taxable income above KRW 300 billion, plus a 10% local income tax surtax on national CIT, producing a 26.4% maximum combined effective corporate tax rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korean Tax Incentive Limitation Law permits R&D tax credits for qualifying software engineering activities; small and medium venture enterprises may enjoy reduced rates; foreign-invested high-tech companies may obtain a 50% corporate tax reduction for up to 5 years if locating in a designated free economic zone; Korea does not operate a patent box regime for software copyright, but R&D deductions and credits substantially lower the effective rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Income Tax Return (Legal Person Tax Base and Amount Calculation Statement) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal, with supporting schedules; the local income tax surtax is reported through the Wetax local tax portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with two provisional CIT prepayment filings during the business year for corporations whose prior tax liability exceeded statutory thresholds.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the return and payment are due by March 31 of the following year. A one-month extension may be granted on reasonable grounds, but overdue interest runs from the original deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business revenue from software development, offshore engineering services, maintenance, licensing, and reimbursed pass-through costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean-resident Chusik Hoesa must report worldwide revenue. A non-resident branch of a foreign corporation must report only Korean-source income. All offshore development revenue attributable to activity in Korea must be included after applying the mandatory transfer pricing adjustment under LCITA Article 4; under-invoicing to a foreign parent is a red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales and operating expenses: payroll, server costs, subcontractor fees, rent, depreciation, and professional fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany subcontracting fees paid to foreign related parties must be backed by contracts, time sheets, and OECD-compliant benchmark data. For a non-resident entity's Korean permanent establishment, only expenses actually incurred for the PE are deductible; allocations from a foreign head office are allowed only to the extent directly related to activities performed in Korea.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible items and tax reconciliation adjustments: entertainment, fines, undocumented cash payments, non-statutory reserves, and excessive related-party management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallowance will be imposed if the Chusik Hoesa cannot provide statutory invoices or electronic tax evidence. Cross-border service payments without substance or economic justification must be added back. This is a common audit focus for offshore development centers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward utilization: offsetting prior-year tax losses against current-year taxable income, limited to the five-year carryforward period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The loss offset is available only if the business continuity requirement is satisfied. A non-resident PE may offset only losses from the same Korean-source business. If there has been a substantial ownership change without continuing business purpose, the loss carryforward will be denied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base for the fiscal year, being taxable income after loss carryforward, tax-exempt income, and non-taxable reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The tax base may not be negative after all offsets. Non-residents cannot use foreign losses to reduce Korean-source offshore engineering income. The amount entered here is the basis for applying progressive corporate tax brackets.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross corporate income tax computed at the statutory progressive brackets: 9% on the first KRW 200 million, 19% on the next KRW 19.8 billion, 21% on the next KRW 280 billion, and 24% on the excess above KRW 300 billion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident with a Korean PE uses the same brackets. If the Korean entity is merely a shell or lacks substantive engineering operations, the tax authority may disregard the entity and re-attribute the entire offshore development income to the beneficial owner, triggering the top effective rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and prepayment offsets: R&D credits, foreign tax credits, provisional payments, and withheld taxes on domestic income received.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The R&D credit requires detailed technical payroll and project records. Foreign tax credits are allowed only where foreign-source income was legally included in the Korean tax base; treaty-related withholding on royalties or interest must be supported by a Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership proof to obtain a reduced rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net corporate tax payable after credits and offsets, together with the local income tax surtax of 10% of national CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The national CIT and local surtax must be paid by the statutory deadline. If the company fails to withhold tax on outbound dividends, interest, or royalties, the payer will be assessed for the unwithheld amount plus additional penalties, and the directors become secondary taxpayers.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and non-filing trigger an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax under National Tax Basic Act Article 47-3; under-reporting triggers 10% of the underpaid tax for negligent filing and 40% for intentional under-reporting under Article 47-2. Unpaid tax accumulates daily overdue interest at the statutory rate. If the evaded corporate tax exceeds KRW 300 million, the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3 imposes aggravated criminal liability of imprisonment for three to five years and a fine of up to three times the tax evaded.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% composite rate on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders: 20% national corporate income tax withholding plus 2% local income tax surtax, unless a bilateral income tax treaty reduces the rate to a lower percentage such as 5%, 10%, or 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding under a Double Tax Agreement, the recipient must provide a current Tax Residency Certificate from the treaty jurisdiction, a beneficial ownership declaration, evidence of substantive business activity, and an ownership/control chart. The Korean payer must file the treaty application with the District Tax Office before payment or, if over-withheld, the recipient must submit a refund claim to the National Tax Service within five years. Treaty relief is denied for conduit arrangements or shell companies lacking economic substance, and for payments to residents who are not the true beneficial owners.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-residents are subject to 22% statutory withholding (20% national plus 2% local); treaty rates typically reduce royalties to 5% to 15%. Interest is also subject to 22% statutory withholding; treaty rates often reduce interest to 0% to 10%. All treaty reductions require compliance with limitation-on-benefits and OECD BEPS Action 6 substance tests.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: The statutory threshold for mandatory Local File preparation and transfer pricing disclosure in Korea is KRW 10 billion of cross-border intercompany transactions per business year; full OECD-aligned Master File and Country-by-Country reporting are required for MNE groups with consolidated revenue above KRW 1 trillion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not use the Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations by name, but substance-over-form, place-of-effective-management, and beneficial ownership rules apply. A Korean offshore development center must maintain real staff, office premises, engineering contracts, payroll records, board minutes, and day-to-day management in Korea. Core Income-Generating Activities must be performed in Korea to qualify for treaty benefits and to avoid having the Chusik Hoesa disregarded as a tax shell.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Shell Company Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Chusik Hoesa is a paper entity with no physical office, no full-time software engineering staff, and no service delivery records in Korea. Board meetings are held abroad, the actual development is performed by offshore subcontractors, and the revenue is booked in a zero-tax jurisdiction while the Korean entity merely functions as an invoicing conduit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3 imposes imprisonment of up to three years or a fine not exceeding twice the amount of tax evaded; where the evaded corporate tax exceeds KRW 300 million, imprisonment is three to five years with a fine up to three times the tax evaded. LCITA Article 4 authorizes the Korean tax office to re-characterize the transaction and disregard the shell entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil will be pierced. Directors are jointly and severally liable for damages under Commercial Act Article 401. National Tax Collection Act Article 39 permits collection of unpaid corporate tax directly from the director's personal assets where default is intentional. Directors are blacklisted as habitual tax delinquents, placed on overseas travel restriction registries, and may be sentenced to criminal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The offshore development center invoices its foreign parent at a nominal 2% net margin without conducting a TNMM or Cost Plus comparability analysis; it pays excessive software royalties or management fees to a related low-tax affiliate; and it fails to maintain a Local File or Master File despite intercompany transactions exceeding KRW 10 billion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under LCITA Article 4, the tax authority adjusts taxable income to the arm's length result. National Tax Basic Act Article 47-2 applies an additional tax of 10% of underpaid tax for unintentional under-reporting and 40% for intentional under-reporting. LCITA Article 11 imposes a documentation failure penalty of up to 2% of the related-party transaction amount, plus statutory daily overdue interest on the deficiency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who approves or signs false pricing documentation and cost-plus calculations is exposed to criminal prosecution under Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3, civil asset restitution under Commercial Act Article 401, and personal collection of additional tax under National Tax Collection Act Article 39. Directors may be blacklisted and prohibited from leaving Korea until the tax liability is settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Evasion and Treaty Abuse on Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean company remits dividends, interest, or software royalties to non-resident shareholders without withholding the statutory 22%, or it mischaracterizes distributions as non-taxable offshore development fees. It also claims a reduced DTA withholding rate using a Tax Residency Certificate from a conduit jurisdiction where the recipient has no substantive operations, no employees, and no true beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate Tax Act Article 76-3 and Local Tax Act Article 103-20 require the payer to remit the unwithheld national and local income tax plus a 10% penalty. LCITA Article 4 denies treaty relief for abusive structures and re-imposes the full 22% statutory rate, with additional tax and penalties for under-reporting. If the false treaty documentation is intentional, criminal sanctions under Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3 also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors act as withholding agents and are personally liable for the unremitted withholding tax, local surtax, and penalties. Their personal assets may be seized, they are blacklisted as delinquent taxpayers, travel bans are issued, and they face criminal imprisonment of up to three years, or up to five years when the tax evaded exceeds KRW 300 million.
